text: Docker Desktop fails to start on Windows when the WSL 2 backend is not installed or is outdated. Open PowerShell as administrator and run `wsl --update` to install the latest WSL kernel. Then restart Docker Desktop and check that the engine status shows running.

If Docker Desktop is stuck on starting, run `wsl --shutdown` to stop all WSL distributions. Restart Docker Desktop afterwards. Virtualization must be enabled in the BIOS for the WSL 2 backend to work.

The error port is already allocated means another container or process is bound to the host port. Run `docker ps` to find the container using the port and stop it with `docker stop`. Alternatively map a different host port with `-p 8081:80`.
To check which process on the host holds the port on Linux, run `sudo lsof -i :8080`. Stop that process or choose another host port when publishing the container port.

The error permission denied while trying to connect to the Docker daemon socket means your user is not in the docker group. Run `sudo usermod -aG docker $USER` to add your user to the docker group. Log out and log back in so that your group membership is re-evaluated.

After adding the user to the docker group, verify that you can run docker commands without sudo by running `docker run hello-world`. If the error persists, check the socket ownership with `ls -l /var/run/docker.sock`.

If a Docker build uses stale layers, rebuild without the cache using `docker build --no-cache .` to force every instruction to run again. Order Dockerfile instructions so that frequently changing files are copied last.

The error failed to solve with frontend dockerfile.v0 usually indicates a syntax error in the Dockerfile or a base image that cannot be pulled. Check the FROM line and confirm the image exists by running `docker pull` for that image.

Services in the same Compose project can reach each other using the service name as the hostname. Do not use localhost to connect from one container to another container. Use the service name, for example db:5432.

The error toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit means anonymous pulls exceeded the Docker Hub limit. Authenticate with `docker login` to receive a higher pull limit. Use a registry mirror for CI systems that pull frequently.
Use named volumes to persist data generated by containers. Removing a container does not remove its named volumes. Run `docker volume ls` to list volumes.

A container that exits with exit code 137 was killed, most often because it ran out of memory. Inspect the container with `docker inspect` and check the OOMKilled field. Increase the memory limit with the `--memory` flag.
